name: infra_fsdp
title: FSDP: auto-wrap policy, bf16 MixedPrecision, sharded state-dict save, set_epoch
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the FSDP script the ROADMAP's framework list names
note: A precision trap with one live false positive. MLV205 fires at line 120 on an accumulation that sits inside `with torch.no_grad():` (line 115). docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 3 says MLV205 fires only when the accumulation 'is not inside a torch.no_grad() scope'; that guard is documented but not implemented - `_accumulations` in analyzer/src/mlview/rules/r_trainloop.py never reads `inside_no_grad`. Under no_grad there is no autograd graph, so the finding's own message ('keeps its autograd graph alive') is false. Recorded as `acceptable` only so this corpus addition does not turn a shared gate red.  UPDATE (hardening round 1, 2026-09-14): the defect named above is fixed, so the rows that were `acceptable` to keep a shared gate green are now `forbidden`, which is what they always should have been.

forbidden.why: the training loader is built with sampler=train_sampler, a DistributedSampler constructed with shuffle=True at line 79
the validation sampler is constructed with shuffle=False at line 80
the module ends in `if __name__ == "__main__": main()` and every loader is built inside main()'s call tree
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called at line 152, before the forward
the order is zero_grad (152) -> forward/loss (153) -> backward (154) -> clip (155) -> step (156)
validate() calls model.eval() at line 112 and restores model.train() at line 124
the validation loop is inside `with torch.no_grad():` at line 115
both loops move tokens and labels with .to(device, non_blocking=True) and the model is moved before FSDP wraps it
every CUDA path in this file is behind torch.cuda.is_available()
seed_all(SEED) at line 130 calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed, torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed_all
there is no sklearn split and no random_split; the DistributedSampler is constructed with an explicit seed=SEED
EncoderBlock.__init__ (line 34) and TinyEncoder.__init__ (line 54) both call super().__init__() as their first statement
the six encoder blocks are held in nn.ModuleList at line 56, so they are registered
the checkpoint is the state dict FSDP.state_dict_type produced, not the module object

the accumulation is inside `with torch.no_grad():` opened at line 115, so no autograd graph exists to keep alive and nothing grows with the epoch. Fixed in hardening round 1 (INFRA-01): `AssignRecord.inside_no_grad` is carried and MLV205 skips it, which is the guard docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 3 always promised.
